findings.finding: The stock is pinned by a completed takeover: HG Projectco 1 (Hunter Group) has >91% at a final NOK 6.30, settlement on 25 Nov and a compulsory acquisition of the remainder at the same NOK 6.30, so from a 6.26 close the window's upside is capped at ~+0.6% and the downside is bounded by a squeeze-out price the offeror is legally committed to; a small drift toward 6.30 as settlement completes inside the window is the lean.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior bid. Post-announcement closes: 5.74 (19 Nov) -> 6.18 (20 Nov) -> 6.25 (23 Nov, 188.5m shares as the block crossed) -> 6.26 (24 Nov), i.e. the spread has narrowed monotonically from 1.9% to 0.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the 0.6% spread to NOK 6.30 is the market's time value to the squeeze-out payment plus a sliver of completion risk. The only unpriced part is the small convergence when settlement (the main completion risk; Hunter reported USD 137.1m cash and working capital on 20 Nov against a ~USD 135m bill for 91%) is confirmed on 25 Nov. If the market doubted settlement the spread would be wider than 0.6%; it is not.
findings.independence: Hunter Group's own Q3 release (cash and working capital USD 137.1m) supports funding from available cash: https://newsweb.oslobors.no/message/687037

findings.finding: Jacktel's Q3 2026 numbers (revenue USD 19.0m, EBITDA USD 10.3m, net profit USD 3.9m, 100% utilisation) were pre-released on 19 Nov inside the bid announcement, so the scheduled report carries nothing new on the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 report +5.62%, Q2 report +2.61%, annual report -1.02% over this stage's window -- all before the bid and no longer relevant to a pinned stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced twice over: the figures are public and the share price is set by the bid, not by earnings.

findings.finding: Jacktel has paid a quarterly USD dividend announced with each report (USD 0.02 ex 22 Apr, USD 0.025 ex 1 Jun announced with Q1, USD 0.03 ex 1 Sep announced with Q2); if the Q3 report declared a similar dividend (~NOK 0.33, ~5% of the price) with a record date the minority could still catch before the squeeze-out, the stock would gap up -- low probability, since the offeror now owns 91% and the squeeze-out follows settlement at a fixed NOK 6.30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dividends were announced with the Q1 and Q2 reports (+5.62% and +2.61% on those days), but never under a bid.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced by being improbable: the bid terms say nothing of a dividend adjustment, and the 0.6% spread shows the market assigns little to it. The finding is a tail only -- a ~5% upside on perhaps a few percent probability.

outside_window.finding: Compulsory acquisition (squeeze-out) at NOK 6.30 under section 4-25 of the Norwegian Limited Liability Companies Act and delisting from Euronext Growth Oslo; minority holders may seek a court valuation, an upside-only option, but none of it resolves within the 25 Nov session.
